summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status skipped). The deterministic gate failed because the custom 2D steady experiment has no floorplan blocks and no power_w object, so input validity failed. simulation_allowed is false, and comparison_valid is false. The scenario is Figure 10 of the 3x3x3 TSV-based 3D-NoC paper, which compares it with a Monolithic 3D-NoC under synthetic traffic at steady state. It uses HotSpot 6.0 with TSV and bonding-layer resistivities and a top heat sink. A planar 2D Studio model cannot represent inter-layer heat flow, TSV conduction, TIM or bonding layers, or the per-layer results. No transient trace applies, since the run would only have been a custom 2D steady one. It is not a bundled EV6/GCC adapted demonstration, and no Ascend910 or ATPlace pinned-size illustrative input.flp or input.ptrace was generated, so there is no source commit or generated placement assumption to report. The only paper observable is the Monolithic maximum of 351.64 K (78.49 C). It is a steady-state HotSpot grid maximum over the hottest Monolithic layer, with the benchmark unnamed. There is no Studio-side value, so no numerical comparison is made, and none would be valid until location, aggregation, regime, and boundary assumptions match. Qualitatively, the paper reports that the hottest TSV-based layer equals the coolest Monolithic layer, which shows the sensitivity of vertical heat paths to bonding layers and TSV conduction. That is a qualitative statement only, with no numeric values published. The final verdict is therefore no simulation and no replication claim, whether exact or approximate.

The paper's system is a 3x3x3 3D stack with TSV and bonding-layer thermal resistivities and a heat sink on top, so it needs a layered 3D thermal model. A 2D single-layer or interposer-style Studio model cannot represent inter-layer heat flow, TSV conduction, bonding/TIM layers, or the per-layer temperature results in Figure 10.

The Monolithic vs TSV comparison depends on removing bonding layers and modifying TSV-area thermal resistivity (Table 3: Copper 0.0025 mK/W, TIM 0.25 mK/W, TSV area 0.0226 mK/W). These material and layer assumptions cannot be reproduced in a planar model.

The paper gives no router coordinates or per-router watts as text, since the per-router synthetic-benchmark powers are only in Figure 8. It publishes only router size, per-router static power and energy per bit, and traffic-scaled power charts. No complete same-scenario floorplan and power set exists.

The paper reports reliability (Black's model MTTF) as a primary outcome. The setup is not a controller or optimizer study, so there is no controller or optimizer to compare, and reliability calculations exceed a simple thermal setup.
The HotSpot 6.0 configuration (heat sink, package, convection, ambient, layer thicknesses) is not published in full, so the solver setup cannot be matched.
